# 4.2.1 Emissions of task-specific and multi-task architectures.

To start our analysis, we examined how the choice of model and architecture type impacts emissions given a specific task and dataset. For this analysis, we took the same 8 task-specific models described in Section 3.2 and compared their emissions to the 8 multi-purpose models described above.

![img-2.jpeg](img-2.jpeg)
Fig. 3. Model emissions (measured in  $\mathrm{g}CO_2eq$ ) and architecture type for each of the datasets from our analysis. The y axis is in logarithmic scale, dot size is proportional to model size.

In Figure 3, we plot the mean query emissions for each model on a dataset-by-dataset basis. We can see that for the two discriminative tasks, sentiment analysis (which includes SST 2, Rotten Tomatoes and IMDB datasets) and question answering (which encompasses SciQ, SQuAD and SQuAD v2) there is a
img_description: The image displays a bubble chart illustrating model emissions in grams of CO2 across different datasets (imdb, sst2, rotten_tomatoes, sciq, squad, squadv2, cnn, samsum, xsum) categorized by architecture type, which includes Task-specific Seq2Seq, Task-specific Encoder, Multi-purpose Decoder, and Multi-purpose Seq2Seq. The size of the bubbles represents the relative emissions, and different colors represent different architecture types, as shown in the legend on the right. The chart highlights that Multi-purpose Seq2Seq architecture generally produces the highest emissions across most datasets.
